headline: Credit card perks drive airline profits as fuel costs rise
pages: Airlines are leaning on loyalty credit cards to offset high jet fuel costs, NPR reported. Banks pay airlines for each account, for miles customers earn and for perks such as lounge access. Analysts say most card spending happens outside the airline brand, as customers collect points. A consumer advocate noted that many rewards are never spent, which is called breakage, and is effectively free money for airlines. Delta said last month that its American Express card program will bring in more than $9 billion this year. The airline predicts a pretax profit of 4.5 billion dollars. One analyst disputed the idea that airlines have become banks, calling it exaggerated.
The programs began 45 years ago with American Airlines' frequent flyer plan. Source: NPR.
